messages:
maria: Heads-up — noticed a 3-5% P90 latency bump over the last deploy for mixed-tenant workloads. Correlation points to continuous-batcher changes + a KV warmup regression. Anyone else seeing this?

lee: saw it in staging. p50 unchanged, but p95/p99 for tenants with long-context profiles spiked.

sasha: I ran a quick flamegraph on the affected slice. Kernel selection stayed on fastpath, but we see more garbage in kv-miss path during batch formation. attaching short log: 
```
[2026-03-18T09:12:03Z] batcher: forming batch (target_tokens=256) tenants=32
[2026-03-18T09:12:03Z] kvcache: miss for tenant T-42, priming async
[2026-03-18T09:12:03Z] scheduler: deferred short requests to wait for kv priming
[2026-03-18T09:12:03Z] kernel: selected cudafast_v2 for seq=1024
```

toni: interesting — deferred short requests? that sounds like long sequences causing short ones to queue and starve. Did quota targets change?

maria: Quote from rollout changelog: "adjust token-budget targets to favor higher aggregate throughput (less aggressive hedging for short sequences)". Maybe that's the culprit.

perf-eng-bot: perf-regression-alert: p99_tail_latency +4.2% in cluster group "mixed-prod-1" after deploy-2026-03-17T23:45

lee: I replayed traces and long sequences are winning the batch credits consistently. Short requests are often delayed waiting for KV cache priming, then they miss the short-path fast kernels.

sasha: Proposed immediate mitigation: re-introduce a proportional short-credit floor per tenant so short requests get a minimum admit rate while their KV priming completes. Something like: `short_floor = max(1, floor(total_budget * 0.08))`

toni: can we do that without blowing throughput? The goal was to reduce context-switch thrash and improve kernel packing.

maria: we could try a hybrid: keep batcher target_tokens=256 but add a soft preempt for short-path candidates that have <128 seq_len and kv_hit_probability > 0.6 — move them ahead of long-path if queueing >50ms.

lee: quick patch I tested in staging: `if short_candidate and wait_ms > 50: promote; promote_limit_per_window=20` results: p95 down ~6% for short tenants, overall p99 neutral, throughput -0.4%.

sasha: logs from that patch show KV priming rate reduced because short requests are sent earlier and hit existing warmed entries more often (less aggregated priming spikes).

infra-bot: note: promoting requests may affect kernel selection docs — ensure kernel fallback still validates for promoted slices.

toni: we should also consider batch formation windowing: dynamic window that closes earlier if short_queue_depth > X. That aligns with proportional admit but preserves batch density for long sequences.

maria: agreed. Action items:
- lee: open canary with short-floor + promote-on-wait (config flag).
- sasha: add telemetry for "promoted_short_hits" and kv_priming_rate per-tenant.
- toni: prototype dynamic-window close heuristic (based on short_queue_depth).

lee: will do. canary target: subset mixed-prod-1 (10% traffic), start 30m ramp.

sasha: also added a small profiler hook to capture kernel selection transitions during promotion so we can verify we still hit fastpath for promoted shorts.

maria: if we see regression on overall p99 we rollback. If short fairness improves with <1% throughput loss, keep and tune.

perf-eng-bot: note: marking this thread linked -> perf/alerts/3712345678

lee: PR opened: https://redwood.internal/pr/4729 (feature: short-floor + promote). comments welcome.

toni: can we add an experiment metric: "tenant-starve-index" = % of short reqs delayed > 100ms / total short reqs ? want to track end-to-end fairness.

maria: yes add that to the dashboard. Sasha, can you add an alert if tenant-starve-index > 2% for >15m?

sasha: on it.

maria: thanks team. will run the canary this afternoon and post results here. :thumbsup:

lee: FYI, I left a small config switch so we can ramp promotion_threshold from 50ms -> 10ms in 3 steps if needed.

maria: Perfect — please annotate the canary with the kernel-profile snapshots so we can correlate.

lee: will do.

sasha: one last note — if promoted shorts still miss kv, we should consider small synchronous priming for short candidates (fire a lightweight kv touch) to reduce subsequent miss cost. but only if telemetry shows priming is cheap for those tenants.

maria: good thought. add as fallthrough plan.

infra-bot: deploy scheduled: canary-4729 -> mixed-prod-1 @ 2026-03-18T16:00 UTC

maria: closing thread for now, will reopen with canary metrics. Thanks all."
